answer: The design leans on time-locked work history, revoked by a single upheld challenge, duplicates are caught by replay, not by name. Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. Reaching the nadir of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. The beacon holds work receipts rather than names, so the lantern of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread.
